subject: physical-education
title: Independent application A: safe rolling and body positions
essentialQuestion: What makes a balance stable, and how do I move my weight safely?
standards: Michigan PE Standard 1: Demonstrates competency in a variety of motor skills and movement patterns
Michigan PE Standard 2: Applies knowledge of concepts, principles, strategies and tactics related to movement and physical activities
Michigan PE Standard 4: Exhibits responsible personal and social behavior that respects self and others

goal: I can supply fresh independent evidence of the taught target for safe rolling and body positions, using a safe standard or equal-credit adapted route, and explain the cue or decision that shows success.
successOverview: Success is safe setup, use of the taught Stable base, comfortable range, continuous breath. cue or decision, a fresh bounded application, and a short explanation. Credit never depends on body position, speed, athletic talent, comparison, or use of the standard route.
readinessCheck: Show the start and finish positions with support and no added load.
Choose movement, seated, supported, mobility-aid, low-space, no-equipment, or described evidence without explaining why.
Use the complete described route if guardian permission, safe space, equipment, movement, a partner, or a real setting is unavailable.
materials: Optional: stable chair, wall, towel, or light adult-approved household object.
Use a smaller lever, gentle isometric action, or hand model of the joint path.
movementCues: Tuck the chin to the chest — never roll on the head or neck.
Curl the back round so you roll smoothly.
Hold the tuck: knees in, hands in.
Roll only on a mat or grass, and only with an adult watching.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Use one short action at a time, say the main cue before the attempt, keep the mastery performance choice concrete, and ask a trusted adult to confirm any required permission or space check.

movementModel.title: Model for safe rolling and body positions
movementModel.startingPosition: Choose a seated, supported, mobility-aid, or standing base with a stable chair or wall positioned before movement.
movementModel.action: Move one joint or body segment through a comfortable range while breathing, pause under control, and return.
movementModel.keyCue: Stable base, comfortable range, continuous breath.
movementModel.commonError: Head contact from an untucked chin. Fix: stop, rebuild the tuck from a seated rock, and progress only when the chin stays down.
movementModel.correction: Reduce range or leverage, remove load, add support, and resume only if comfortable.
movementModel.notice: Notice alignment, breathing, and controlled return rather than depth, load, or duration.
movementModel.adaptedModel: Use the seated, supported, mobility-aid, reduced-range, object-modeled, or described route and preserve this evidence: Notice alignment, breathing, and controlled return rather than depth, load, or duration.
movementModel.safetyBoundary: Use stable supports and learner-selected range; stop before alignment or breathing breaks down. No maximal resistance, forced stretch, inversion, breath-holding, unstable support, or movement through pain.

guidedPractice.support: Use the model cue: Stable base, comfortable range, continuous breath.
guidedPractice.feedback: If the target is unclear, return to the starting position and use this correction: Reduce range or leverage, remove load, add support, and resume only if comfortable.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete one comfortable controlled movement or isometric shape while breathing.
guidedPractice.support: Watch for this contrast: Increasing range, load, or hold time after alignment or breathing changes.
guidedPractice.feedback: Keep the safe version when the learner can show or explain notice alignment, breathing, and controlled return rather than depth, load, or duration.

directions: Choose a fresh comfortable variation and show or describe stable base, alignment, breath, and controlled return.

independentActivity.freshTask: Complete a fresh bounded application without answer-bearing coaching; receive feedback only after the evidence is supplied. Choose a fresh comfortable variation and show or describe stable base, alignment, breath, and controlled return.
independentActivity.independenceBoundary: A trusted human or future Tutor may read directions, define a cue, and offer an approved route. They may not perform the decision for the learner, claim unapproved observation, certify physical completion, or provide medical or return clearance.

warmUp: Move the target joint through a small comfortable range.
Rehearse the breathing and return cue with support.
coolDown: Return to the easiest comfortable version or rest.
Restore optional equipment and space safely.
Name one cue, safety choice, or next adjustment without reporting body data.

spaceSetup: Clear one arm-span on a dry non-slip surface and place any stable support before beginning. Do not use rolling or tipping furniture. Low-space access remains available before and during the lesson. Cleanup: return optional items only after movement has stopped and the path is clear.

optional: Optional: stable chair, wall, towel, or light adult-approved household object.
householdSubstitutes: Use a smaller lever, gentle isometric action, or hand model of the joint path.
prohibited: No maximal resistance, forced stretch, inversion, breath-holding, unstable support, or movement through pain.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit no-equipment route: use a seated, supported, reduced-range, or gentle isometric version, or model the joint path with hands while explaining alignment and breathing.

safetyRules: Check the surface, ceiling, boundary, people, pets, cords, breakables, footwear or mobility supports, and any optional item before movement.
Use stable supports and learner-selected range; stop before alignment or breathing breaks down.
Use learner-selected range, pace, and demand. Control, decisions, and understanding matter more than force, distance, duration, or repetitions.
If the environment cannot be made safe, do not perform movement; use the equal-credit described route or stop and tell a trusted adult.
stoppingRules: REST / ADJUST: You may pause, rest, reduce pace or range, use support, switch to an approved route, or finish for the day at any time. You may resume only when comfortable and the environment is safe. Rest and adaptation never reduce credit.

STOP AND TELL: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, an injury concern, damaged equipment, or an unsafe environment. Tell a trusted adult and do not continue to test the concern.

DO NOT RESUME: After a head impact, an injury concern, or a symptom that persists or worsens, remain out until the authorized guardian or qualified professional says it is safe. A learner, browser, or Tutor cannot provide clearance.

adaptationRoutes.supported: Place an approved stable support before beginning and use it through the whole attempt; score the cue or decision for safe rolling and body positions, not unsupported balance.
adaptationRoutes.reducedRange: Use the smallest comfortable movement, eye-gaze choice, point, or gesture that still shows the target cue or decision for safe rolling and body positions.
adaptationRoutes.reducedPaceOrDemand: Complete one stage at a time with learner-chosen breaks, remain at the entry version, or split the lesson across short sittings.
adaptationRoutes.mobilityAidCompatible: Keep the mobility aid positioned and used as approved; adapt the path around the aid and score the same Stable base, comfortable range, continuous breath. evidence.
adaptationRoutes.solo: Use the supplied solo, shadow, diagram, imagined-role, or fictional-situation route; no partner, opponent, group, or audience is required.
adaptationRoutes.lowSpace: Use the one-arm-span or one-seat setup: Equal-credit no-equipment route: use a seated, supported, reduced-range, or gentle isometric version, or model the joint path with hands while explaining alignment and breathing.
adaptationRoutes.noEquipment: Equal-credit no-equipment route: use a seated, supported, reduced-range, or gentle isometric version, or model the joint path with hands while explaining alignment and breathing.

retryPlan.trigger: Retry when the evidence does not yet show the target cue or decision for safe rolling and body positions; name the missing observable part without judging the learner.
retryPlan.simplerSetup: Show the start and finish positions with support and no added load.
retryPlan.differentCue: Replace the full cue set with: “Stable base, comfortable range, continuous breath.”
retryPlan.alternateModel: Contrast this common error — Increasing range, load, or hold time after alignment or breathing changes. — with this correction — Reduce range or leverage, remove load, add support, and resume only if comfortable.
retryPlan.boundedPractice: Complete one comfortable controlled movement or isometric shape while breathing.
retryPlan.freshRetry: Choose a fresh comfortable variation and show or describe stable base, alignment, breath, and controlled return. Use a new safe example rather than repeating the scored attempt.
retryPlan.exitCriterion: Return to independent work when the fresh retry shows or explains notice alignment, breathing, and controlled return rather than depth, load, or duration. A safety stop, rest, or adaptation is never recorded as failure.

guardianAuthority.when: Guardian permission is required before real movement, optional equipment, a real location, partner, outdoor route, or progression is used.
guardianAuthority.requiredAction: The guardian confirms that the bounded space, optional equipment, and activity route are permitted before movement.
guardianAuthority.minimumRecord: Record only permission status or that the equal-credit described route was used; collect no body, health, media, location, or performance data.
guardianAuthority.confirmationBoundary: Guardian confirmation may establish permission or occurrence only. It does not certify academic mastery, physical quality, diagnosis, effort, body status, or safe return.
guardianAuthority.equalCreditAlternative: When guardian review, real movement, equipment, space, partner, or location is unavailable, the supplied solo described/decision route is the complete equal-credit lesson.
